messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the service-actor RFC — thinking about collapsing project-scoped service keys into a single canonical service identity (service://) and mapping project bindings via RBAC instead of separate key namespaces. pros/cons? ravi: I'm +1 on simplifying the surface. Main worry is accidental cross-project access during migration. How do we preserve least-privilege while we transition? :thinking_face: ellie: Migration plan could use an intermediate validation layer: when a service key is presented, check both the old project-scoped mapping and the new canonical identity. Emit telemetry and a soft-deny header for mismatches. ben: Right. Also we need to think about tooling: devs currently see keys in project settings. If we move to service identities, UI needs to show per-project role bindings for each service. That's a UX lift. maya: Agreed on UX. Operationally I want to avoid adding a new global lookup per request. Can we keep token format including a short project tag so runtime routing stays cheap? e.g. `svc-+p:` in token metadata. ravi: That sounds like a compromise. But then token becomes coupled to project again. Might defeat simplification. What's the win vs complexity tradeoff? ellie: The win is reducing key churn and making service identity stable across infra changes. Complexity shows up in authz: we must be able to author role bindings anchored to (service, project) tuples. ben: If we do role bindings at (service, project) tuple, we preserve current semantics but use a single canonical key so rotation is easier. Also simpler for dedicated/private: customers can pin service identity. sec-bot: deploy-checklist triggered: remember to add compatibility feature-flag for the auth layer when rolling out. maya: On perf: propose a tiny in-memory cache mapping presented key -> resolved (service, project, roleset) with LRU TTL 2m. That avoids DB hop for steady-state. ravi: Cache good. Add audit counters for ‘resolved-by-old-mapping’ vs ‘resolved-by-new-identity’. We'll need regression alerts if old mappings drop to zero too fast. ellie: Edgecases: background jobs that run cross-project (billing, infra reconciliation). They often rely on project-scoped tokens. For those we either keep old keys until jobs are migrated or add explicit cross-project role. maya: Migration steps sketch: 1) introduce canonical service identity + dual-resolution (old and new) behind flag; 2) emit telemetry + warning header; 3) surface bindings UI; 4) run canary for non-critical services; 5) flip default to new resolution; 6) deprecate old mapping after 90d. ben: Also add a compatibility mode for Dedicated/Private where customers can opt into map-only migration window; they might need longer than 90d. ravi: Security check: rotation and revocation semantics must remain per-service. If a service key is compromised, we need immediate revocation across all projects. That is easier with canonical identity. ellie: One open question: do we allow creating project-scoped ephemeral tokens derived from the canonical identity for short-lived ops? (like `svc:::proj:

::exp:1h`). That helps least-privilege for CI. maya: I like ephemeral derived tokens. Implementation: mint signed JWTs by auth-service with `sub=svc:`, `aud=project:

`, short exp, and include `x-derivation: canonical->project`. Runtime verifies signature and enforces aud. ravi: Implementation note: need to ensure libraries can validate quickly. We already have JWT verification in runtime so reuse that path. Telemetry needs to mark derived tokens for traceability. ben: Ok next: DB model change. Current table: `service_keys(project_id, key_id, secret_hash, meta)`. New model: `services(id, canonical_meta)` + `service_bindings(service_id, project_id, roleset)`. Migration script must backfill bindings and keep key entries referencing service_id. ellie: We should add a migration-mode flag on auth-service so old endpoints still read `service_keys` directly until cutover. maya: Final asks before RFC update: - add sample token formats in RFC - define canary checklist (routes, metrics, fallback policy) - security review for derived token design ravi: I'll draft a short canary checklist and add the audit counters + alert thresholds. ben: I'll mock the UI wire for bindings and add to the RFC. ellie: I'll write the migration playbook and DB diff. maya: Thanks team. Putting this as a follow-up to the RFC. Will update the doc with those pieces and the rollout timeline. :thumbsup:
